# Welcome {-}  
  
These are the first-semester lecture notes for **MFE 813: Regulation  
of Financial Markets & Institutions**, a course in the Masters in  
Financial Economics programme at Kaduna State University. The course  
examines how financial markets and institutions are regulated — in the  
Nigerian domestic environment and in the international system.  
  
## What this book covers  
  
- **Chapter \@ref(chap-nfs) — The Nigerian Financial System**: the  
  meaning of financial institutions and regulation, an overview of the  
  banking sector, the nature of financial systems (risk, asymmetric  
  information, interdependence, money), and the history of banking in  
  Nigeria.  
- **Chapter \@ref(chap-instability) — Instability and Regulatory  
  Responses**: sources of instability in the banking system, the  
  regulatory authorities' stabilisation efforts, emerging issues and  
  challenges, and possible remedial actions.  
- **Chapter \@ref(chap-domestic) — Domestic Regulatory  
  Institutions**: the objectives of financial regulation and the roles  
  of the CBN, NDIC, SEC, and NAICOM.  
- **Chapter \@ref(chap-intl) — International Dimensions**:  
  international financial market difficulties and the International  
  Monetary Fund (IMF).  
- **Appendix**: summary tables of regulators and full references.  
  
## Course outline {-}  
  
The course covers four policy study areas:  
  
1. Issues in the Nigerian financial system  
2. Regulatory institutions in the domestic environment  
   (CBN, NDIC, SEC, NAICOM)  
3. International dimensions of financial regulation  
   (IMF, World Bank, AfDB)  
4. Economic stabilisation measures  
   (monetary policy, fiscal policy, direct controls)  
  
:::{.rmdnote}  
These notes are issued per semester. Units still to be added this  
semester: the World Bank (IBRD), the African Development Bank, and the  
economic stabilisation instruments.  
:::  
  
:::{.rmdimportant}  
These are lecture notes intended to support classroom teaching for MFE  
813. They supplement — not replace — the readings listed in the  
References section.  
:::
